chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Band members' schooling, trumpet chops and Hot Lips' lip
summary: Only Lewis, Page and Coleman had been to school; Hot Lips took many choruses and toughened his lip with a salve.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: All these young guys, like yourself and the others in the
Buster Smith - 46
Blue Devils, taking the average, how they learned music... Had any of them studied music?
Had any of them been to school?
Yes. Some of them had. Now, Willie Lewis and Walter Page had been to school, and I think Coleman (that's the one we called Buckets), he was the first bandleader....
Ermir Coleman.
Yes. He had been to school. The rest of them boys just picked it up.
One of the things that I'm particularly interested in is trumpet players, because the trumpet is a really hard instrument to play.
Yes.
It's an instrument where there's a tremendous physical thing, quite apart from the music. It's actually very hard to blow and to get a good tone and that.
Yeah, that's true.
Were there any good teachers around? Did any of the guys sort of go and study with somebody to get some help with that and get their chops in shape?
Not in the Blue Devils band. Not while I was there. They didn't take time ...(?)...
Did the guys ever have problems? Did you get times where
Buster Smith - 47
one of the trumpet players would lose his lip or he'd get like physical problems?

Yeah, yeah. Well, we had two or three around then. Let me see. Smith, I can't think of his first name.... He was a (?) trumpet player. He didn't stay in the band long. He died, too. Good trumpet player. Now, he's right on with a (?)whole list(?) of boys. That Joe Keyes and Hot Lips, Leroy White, they was all in good health, all the time. Yeah. All the time.
I mean, apparently Hot Lips used to take ten or fifteen choruses all the time.
Yeah!
Well, you know, to keep that sort of thing up night after night after night, you've got to have some chops.
Yeah.
He never had any problems?
No, he didn't. He used to complain about his lip getting sore, but he'd put some Calfinique(?) on it and go right on playing.
Put what on it?
Calfinique(?). That toughens your lip.
Really.
Yeah. It toughens your lip.
I'd think it would damage your lip, too.
